name: Semaglutide

chain: Calorie deficit and lower body fat
angle.text: Users take semaglutide to lose body fat quickly, which also slims the face and reduces puffiness. Forum posters also discuss "Ozempic face" hollowing and muscle loss. Weight loss is well studied in trials; the facial effects are reported anecdotally and in case discussions rather than measured.

summary: GLP-1 agonist that kills appetite → major weight loss. The face leans out as the body does.
note: Does not target face fat specifically — facial change rides along with total fat loss.
currentQuick:
Semaglutide is a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist developed by Novo Nordisk. It is marketed as Ozempic and Rybelsus for type 2 diabetes and as Wegovy for chronic weight management, and it is given as a weekly injection or, in the case of Rybelsus, a daily tablet.
In appearance-focused communities it is used as a fat-loss drug: large reductions in appetite produce substantial total weight loss, and the face usually leans out along with the body. The drug has no known ability to target facial fat specifically; the so-called Ozempic face is generally explained as the effect of rapid overall fat and volume loss, particularly in older people, rather than a distinct action of the molecule.
How it works: Semaglutide mimics the gut hormone GLP-1, binding GLP-1 receptors in the brain's appetite centres and in the pancreas. It reduces hunger and increases satiety, slows gastric emptying, and enhances glucose-dependent insulin secretion while suppressing glucagon. A fatty-acid side chain lets it bind albumin, which extends its half-life enough for once-weekly dosing. Weight loss follows mainly from lower energy intake.
Risks and caveats: Gastrointestinal effects such as nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation are the most common problems, and rarer events include gallbladder disease and pancreatitis. It carries a boxed warning about thyroid C-cell tumours seen in rodents. Substantial lean mass can be lost along with fat unless protein intake and resistance training are maintained, and weight is typically regained after stopping. It is prescription-only; compounded and grey-market versions of uncertain quality are widely sold and raise separate safety concerns. Facial hollowing and sagging can occur with fast, large weight loss.
deepLead:
Semaglutide is a peptide medication that mimics the gut hormone glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and acts as a GLP-1 receptor agonist. Developed by Novo Nordisk, it is sold as Ozempic and Rybelsus for type 2 diabetes and as Wegovy for chronic weight management, and is given as a weekly injection or, in the case of the oral products, a daily tablet . It was approved in the United States in 2017 and in Canada, the European Union and Japan in 2018 .
In clinical trials of adults with overweight or obesity and no diabetes, semaglutide at the 2.4 mg weekly dose produced average weight reductions in the range of roughly 12 percent of body weight over 68 weeks or longer, compared with small losses on placebo . Large outcome trials have also reported lower rates of major cardiovascular events in people with diabetes and in people with obesity and established cardiovascular disease .
In looksmaxxing communities, semaglutide is discussed as a systemic fat-loss tool whose effects on the face follow overall fat loss; the drug has no known mechanism for targeting facial fat specifically. The phrase "Ozempic face" describes the gaunt or hollowed facial appearance that some people report after large, rapid weight loss on GLP-1 drugs . Documented adverse effects are mainly gastrointestinal, and the US label carries a boxed warning about thyroid C-cell tumors seen in rodents . Unregulated or compounded semaglutide products are also discussed online.

name: Tirzepatide

angle.text: Users take tirzepatide to cut body fat, often claiming it works better than semaglutide, with the face leaning out as weight falls. Trials show large weight loss in people with obesity. Appearance outcomes such as facial leanness or muscle retention are untested and based on anecdote.

summary: Dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist — the biggest trial weight losses of any approved drug.
currentQuick:
Tirzepatide is a once-weekly injectable from Eli Lilly that activates both the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and GLP-1 receptors. It is sold as Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes and as Zepbound for chronic weight management, and in phase 3 trials it produced the largest average weight reductions of any approved anti-obesity drug.
In looksmaxxing communities it is used as a systemic fat-loss drug. As with other incretin drugs, facial leaning follows total fat loss rather than being targeted, and because the weight loss is larger, facial volume loss and skin laxity can be more noticeable in some users.
How it works: Tirzepatide is a modified peptide that acts as an agonist at the GIP and GLP-1 receptors, with stronger activity at GIP. GLP-1 signalling reduces appetite, slows gastric emptying and supports insulin secretion; GIP signalling is thought to add to appetite suppression and may improve tolerability and adipose tissue handling. The combined effect lowers calorie intake and improves glycaemic control.
Risks and caveats: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation are common, mostly during dose escalation. Pancreatitis, gallbladder disease and dehydration-related kidney injury have been reported, and the label carries a thyroid C-cell tumour warning. It can reduce the effectiveness of oral contraceptives. Lean mass loss accompanies fat loss, and weight returns after discontinuation. It is prescription-only; unregulated peptide-vial sources add contamination and dosing-accuracy risks.
deepLead:
Tirzepatide is an injectable peptide that activates both the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptor and the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor. Made by Eli Lilly, it is given once weekly and sold as Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes and as Zepbound for chronic weight management and, in the United States, moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea .
In the SURMOUNT-1 phase 3 trial of adults with obesity or overweight without diabetes, mean weight change at 72 weeks was about -15.0, -19.5 and -20.9 percent at the 5, 10 and 15 mg weekly doses . These are among the largest average reductions reported for an approved anti-obesity drug, and in a 2025 head-to-head trial it was compared directly with semaglutide .
Looksmaxxing communities discuss tirzepatide as a systemic fat-loss tool; facial leaning follows overall fat loss rather than being targeted. Its documented adverse effects are mostly gastrointestinal, and the US label carries a boxed warning on thyroid C-cell tumors observed in rodents . Weight regain after stopping is documented, and forum users also discuss unregulated peptide supplies, whose contents are not verified by regulators.

name: Liraglutide

angle.text: Liraglutide is a daily GLP-1 injection that users discuss as an older, milder fat-loss option than semaglutide. It is used to cut body fat. Weight-loss effects are studied in trials; claims about muscle sparing or dosing around cravings are anecdotal.

summary: Daily-injection GLP-1; older and less potent than semaglutide.
currentQuick:
Liraglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist from Novo Nordisk, given as a daily injection. It was approved as Victoza for type 2 diabetes and, at a higher strength, as Saxenda for chronic weight management; it was the first GLP-1 drug approved for obesity treatment.
Its weight-loss effect is more modest than that of semaglutide or tirzepatide, with average losses in trials of roughly 5 to 8 percent of body weight. It is now of mainly historical or niche interest in fat-loss circles, as newer agents with larger reported effects have largely replaced it.
How it works: Liraglutide is a GLP-1 analogue with a fatty-acid chain that promotes albumin binding and gives it a half-life of about 13 hours, allowing once-daily dosing. By activating GLP-1 receptors it increases satiety, delays gastric emptying and enhances glucose-dependent insulin release, which lowers calorie intake and body weight.
Risks and caveats: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation are the usual complaints, with gallbladder events, pancreatitis and raised heart rate reported less often. It carries a boxed warning about thyroid C-cell tumours in rodents. Weight is commonly regained when the drug is stopped, and it requires daily injections. It is prescription-only.
deepLead:
Liraglutide is a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist made by Novo Nordisk and given by daily subcutaneous injection. Under the brand name Victoza it is used for type 2 diabetes, and at a higher strength as Saxenda it is used for chronic weight management; it is also available as a generic . It was approved in the European Union in 2009 and in the United States in 2010 .
Its weight-loss effect in trials is smaller than that of the newer weekly drugs semaglutide and tirzepatide. Wikipedia describes liraglutide as less effective than standard-dose semaglutide for weight loss, and the STEP 8 trial compared the two directly . In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums it is discussed mostly as an older, shorter-acting alternative that some users prefer because the daily schedule lets them time doses .
The US label has a boxed warning about thyroid C-cell tumors seen in rodents, and other labelled risks include pancreatitis, hypoglycemia with some other diabetes drugs, and acute kidney injury from volume depletion .

name: Retatrutide

angle.text: Retatrutide is an investigational drug that users source as research peptides, hoping for the largest fat loss yet and sometimes stack with TRT or anabolics. Trials report large weight loss but it is unapproved. Use for body recomposition and the equivalence of vials to trial drug are untested.

summary: Triple GLP-1/GIP/glucagon agonist in trials. Huge early numbers, still investigational.
currentQuick:
Retatrutide (LY3437943) is an investigational once-weekly injectable from Eli Lilly that activates three receptors: GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon. It has not been approved by any regulator and is being studied for obesity, type 2 diabetes and related conditions.
Phase 2 data showed average weight loss of about 24 percent at 48 weeks at the highest dose, the largest figure reported for a drug of this type at that stage. Interest in looksmaxxing communities has driven a grey market of research-labelled vials, which carry quality and safety risks that trial participants do not face.
How it works: The GIP and GLP-1 components reduce appetite and improve glucose handling as with tirzepatide. The added glucagon-receptor agonism is thought to raise energy expenditure and increase fat oxidation in the liver, which may also reduce liver fat. The three-way action is intended to produce greater weight loss than dual or single agonists.
Risks and caveats: Reported trial effects are mostly gastrointestinal and dose-related, with some increases in heart rate, and long-term safety is not yet established. Because it is unapproved, any retatrutide sold outside trials is unregulated: purity, identity and dose are unverified, and use is outside the law in many jurisdictions. The same lean-mass loss and weight regain concerns that apply to other incretin drugs are expected to apply here.
deepLead:
Retatrutide (development code LY3437943) is an investigational once-weekly injectable peptide from Eli Lilly that activates three receptors: glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucagon . It is being studied for obesity, type 2 diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea, knee osteoarthritis and fatty liver disease, and as of the sources reviewed it has no regulatory approval .
In a phase 2 obesity trial published in 2023, retatrutide produced large dose-related weight loss in adults without diabetes . Phase 3 results published in 2026 reported mean weight reductions of 17.6, 23.7 and 25.0 percent at 4, 9 and 12 mg after 80 weeks, versus 3.9 percent for placebo, according to Wikipedia's summary of the TRIUMPH-1 trial . Reported adverse effects are mainly gastrointestinal and dose-related, with some mild heart-rate increases .
In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities, retatrutide is discussed as a more powerful fat-loss peptide than semaglutide or tirzepatide. Because it is unapproved, supplies outside trials are sold by research-chemical vendors whose products are not regulated, and Wikipedia reports that Lilly has filed lawsuits against black-market sellers .

name: Cagrilintide

angle.text: Cagrilintide is an experimental amylin analogue that users discuss alone or with semaglutide as a strong appetite suppressant for getting lean. It is in clinical trials and unapproved on its own. Fat loss is studied in trial populations; looks-focused "leanmaxxing" claims are opinion.

summary: Long-acting amylin analogue that suppresses appetite; trialed combined with semaglutide (CagriSema).
currentQuick:
Cagrilintide is a long-acting analogue of amylin, a hormone co-secreted with insulin that signals fullness. Developed by Novo Nordisk, it is injected once weekly and is under investigation for obesity, both alone and fixed-dose combined with semaglutide as CagriSema.
It is not approved as a standalone product. Its role in appearance contexts is as another systemic fat-loss agent still within the clinical-development pipeline, and research-labelled supplies appear on the grey market.
How it works: Cagrilintide activates amylin and calcitonin receptors in the brain, notably in the hindbrain, reducing appetite and food intake and slowing gastric emptying. Because its pathway differs from GLP-1, it is combined with semaglutide with the aim of additive weight loss.
Risks and caveats: Trial reports describe mainly gastrointestinal effects such as nausea and vomiting, which are dose-related. Long-term safety is still being assessed and it is unapproved as a single agent. Unregulated research-chemical products are of unverified quality. Evidence here is limited to company-sponsored trial publications and press releases.
deepLead:
Cagrilintide is a long-acting analogue of amylin, a pancreatic hormone co-secreted with insulin that promotes satiety. Developed by Novo Nordisk, it is injected once weekly and is being tested for obesity and type 2 diabetes, both alone and in a fixed combination with semaglutide called CagriSema . It is not approved as a standalone product in the sources reviewed.
A 2021 phase 2 trial examined dose-response effects of once-weekly cagrilintide on body weight in people with overweight or obesity . Wikipedia reports that in the REDEFINE 1 study cagrilintide alone produced a mean body-weight reduction of 11.8 percent versus 2.3 percent for placebo after 68 weeks, and that 31.6 percent of participants lost at least 15 percent of body weight . Phase 3 results of the combination with semaglutide were published in 2025 .
In appearance-oriented contexts cagrilintide is another systemic fat-loss agent in the clinical pipeline. The sources reviewed contain no forum or practitioner material on it, and the evidence is limited to company-sponsored trial publications and reviews.

name: Setmelanotide

chain: Less hunger in rare genetic obesity
angle.text: Setmelanotide is approved only for obesity from rare genetic pathway disorders, so its appearance link is indirect: it is mentioned in fat-loss peptide discussions. Its weight effects are studied in those specific patients; use for ordinary fat loss in otherwise healthy people is untested.

summary: MC4R agonist for obesity caused by rare genetic conditions.
note: Only for those specific genetic conditions.
currentQuick:
Setmelanotide (Imcivree) is a melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R) agonist from Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, given by daily injection. It is approved for severe obesity caused by specific rare genetic conditions, including POMC, PCSK1 and LEPR deficiency and Bardet-Biedl syndrome.
It is a rare-disease therapy rather than a general weight-loss drug, and no established role has been shown for people whose obesity has common causes. It appears in looksmaxxing discussions mainly as an example of targeted pharmacology.
How it works: Setmelanotide stimulates MC4R in the hypothalamus, a key point in the leptin-melanocortin pathway that controls hunger and energy expenditure. In people whose genetic defect disrupts upstream signalling, direct MC4R activation can restore satiety signalling and reduce hunger.
Risks and caveats: Common effects include injection-site reactions, skin darkening, nausea and spontaneous penile erections or sexual arousal effects, and depression and suicidal ideation are monitored. It is prescription-only and approved only for confirmed genetic diagnoses, so use for ordinary obesity is off-label and has no supporting evidence.
deepLead:
Setmelanotide, sold as Imcivree, is a melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R) agonist given by daily subcutaneous injection. It was invented at Ipsen and developed by Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, and it is approved for obesity caused by rare genetic or acquired disorders of the leptin-melanocortin pathway . It was approved in the United States in November 2020 and in the European Union in July 2021 and the FDA considers it first-in-class .
The current US label covers adults and children with acquired hypothalamic obesity (aged 4 and over) and with syndromic or monogenic obesity due to Bardet-Biedl syndrome or genetically confirmed POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency (aged 2 and over) . It is not approved for ordinary polygenic obesity .
Setmelanotide is not a general weight-loss drug, and the sources reviewed contain no looksmaxxing community discussion of it. It is included because it is an example of targeted pharmacology in the obesity field.

name: Tesamorelin

angle.text: Tesamorelin is a prescription GHRH analogue that users, often with ipamorelin, take to lose fat and raise IGF-1. It is approved for abdominal fat in HIV lipodystrophy. Use in healthy people for physique or facial leanness is off-label and largely anecdotal.

summary: GHRH analogue that cuts visceral belly fat in specific HIV patients.
note: Cannot selectively remove cheek or jawline fat.
currentQuick:
Tesamorelin (Egrifta) is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone approved in the United States to reduce excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy. It is injected daily.
It is sometimes discussed in body-composition and peptide circles for visceral fat reduction. Its approval and evidence cover only that specific patient group, and it has not been shown to remove fat from the cheeks or jawline selectively.
How it works: Tesamorelin stimulates the pituitary to release endogenous growth hormone in a pulsatile fashion, which raises IGF-1. Growth hormone promotes lipolysis, with a particular effect on visceral adipose tissue, which explains the reduction in trunk fat in trials.
Risks and caveats: Reported effects include joint pain, fluid retention, injection-site reactions and glucose intolerance, and raised IGF-1 prompts caution about malignancy. It is prescription-only and costly, fat returns after stopping, and benefits in people without HIV lipodystrophy are not established.
deepLead:
Tesamorelin (brand names Egrifta, Egrifta SV and Egrifta WR) is a synthetic analogue of growth-hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) made by Theratechnologies of Canada. It was approved by the US FDA in November 2010 for reducing excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy and is given by daily subcutaneous injection .
It stimulates the pituitary to release endogenous growth hormone in a pulsatile pattern, raising IGF-1 and promoting lipolysis, with a particular effect on visceral fat . The label states it is not indicated for weight loss management, as its effect on weight is neutral, and that long-term cardiovascular safety has not been established .
In bodybuilding and peptide forums it is discussed as a growth-hormone secretagogue, often paired with ipamorelin, for fat loss and raising IGF-1 . Approval and trial evidence cover HIV-associated abdominal fat; the drug is not known to remove fat from the face or any specific site selectively, and benefits in people without HIV lipodystrophy have not been established in the cited trials.

name: AOD-9604

angle.text: AOD-9604 is a growth hormone fragment sold as a research peptide that users take for fat loss without GH side effects, often stacked with other peptides. It was tested for obesity in humans with disappointing results. Its looks-related effects are claimed mainly on forums.

summary: Modified GH fragment marketed for fat loss. Human efficacy evidence came up short.
currentQuick:
AOD-9604 is a synthetic peptide derived from the fat-metabolising region of human growth hormone, a modified version of its C-terminal fragment. It was developed in Australia as an obesity treatment and later sold as a research peptide for fat loss.
Human trials in obesity did not show clinically meaningful weight loss, and the developer discontinued the obesity program. It continues to be promoted in peptide marketing, although efficacy evidence in humans is limited.
How it works: The peptide is proposed to mimic the lipolytic action of growth hormone without its effects on growth or blood sugar, stimulating fat breakdown and inhibiting fat formation in adipose tissue. Evidence for this comes from cell and animal studies, and the effect was not robustly observed in humans.
Risks and caveats: Short-term safety in clinical studies was described as similar to placebo, but long-term data are lacking. It is not approved as a drug in most countries, is sold as a research chemical of variable quality, and is prohibited in competitive sport by WADA. Human trials have not shown a clinically meaningful fat-loss benefit.
deepLead:
AOD-9604 is a 16-amino-acid synthetic peptide based on residues 176 to 191 of human growth hormone (hGH), with a tyrosine substituted for the N-terminal phenylalanine. It was developed as a potential obesity treatment on the idea that this fragment retains growth hormone's fat-metabolizing action without its other effects .
Metabolic Pty developed it in Australia, with phase IIa trials underway by 2002 . Wikipedia reports that early human trials suggested lipolytic activity without IGF-1 stimulation, that a 12-week randomized trial found participants lost on average 1.8 kg more than placebo, and that a later 24-week trial showed poor efficacy and development ended in 2007 .
It is not an approved drug in the sources reviewed. It is sold by research-peptide vendors for fat loss and is listed as prohibited by anti-doping rules . Sources reviewed include only a single brief forum mention of its use .

name: HGH Fragment 176-191

angle.text: HGH Fragment 176-191 is sold as a research chemical and discussed in bodybuilding forums as a way to mobilize fat like growth hormone without its growth effects. Users stack it with secretagogues or stimulants. Evidence is preclinical; human fat-loss data are lacking.

summary: GH fragment promoted for lipolysis. Preclinical only.
currentQuick:
HGH Fragment 176-191 is a 16-amino-acid peptide corresponding to the C-terminal end of human growth hormone. It is sold as a research chemical and promoted for fat loss on the idea that it keeps growth hormone's lipolytic action without its other effects.
Published data are largely preclinical, and no completed controlled human trials of this exact peptide support its marketing claims. Its modified relative AOD-9604 did reach human trials but fell short on efficacy.
How it works: In cell and rodent studies the fragment appears to stimulate lipolysis and reduce lipogenesis in fat tissue, apparently without activating the growth hormone receptor pathways that raise IGF-1 or blood glucose. The exact receptor mechanism is not well defined.
Risks and caveats: Human safety data are essentially absent for this specific peptide. It is unapproved for medical use, supplied by unregulated sources with unverified purity, and listed as prohibited by WADA among growth hormone fragments. Efficacy for human fat loss is unproven.
deepLead:
HGH Fragment 176-191 (also written hGH frag 176-191 or "frag") is a synthetic peptide that corresponds to the final sixteen amino acids at the C-terminal end of the 191-residue human growth hormone molecule. It is sold online as a research chemical and is discussed in bodybuilding and fat-loss forums as a way to obtain growth hormone's fat-mobilising action without its growth-promoting effects.
The idea behind the product comes largely from research on AOD9604, a modified version of the same segment that was tested in humans. Wikipedia notes that the unmodified fragment has been presented as lipolytic by extrapolation from AOD9604 data and that, unlike AOD9604, it has not itself been studied in humans. Published work on the fragment is mostly laboratory and animal research, and it is not approved as a medicine.
In community discussion it appears in bodybuilding contest-prep logs alongside other peptides, stimulants and thyroid hormone, usually as an add-on for cutting phases.

name: 5-Amino-1MQ

angle.text: 5-Amino-1MQ is a gray-market small molecule that users take to raise fat metabolism and lose body fat. It is not a peptide, despite how it is sold. Evidence is limited to cell and animal studies; human fat-loss and safety data are absent.

summary: NNMT inhibitor marketed for fat metabolism. Preclinical.
currentQuick:
5-Amino-1MQ is a small-molecule inhibitor of nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT), an enzyme that is more active in fat tissue in obesity. It is marketed online as an oral or injectable fat-metabolism supplement.
The evidence is confined to cell and mouse experiments, and no human trials have been published. Its use in looksmaxxing rests on extrapolation from these preclinical results.
How it works: Inhibiting NNMT is thought to raise cellular NAD+ levels and the availability of methyl donors, which in mouse adipocytes shifted metabolism towards energy use and reduced fat cell size. In diet-induced obese mice, NNMT inhibitors reduced weight and fat mass, an effect that has not been confirmed in humans.
Risks and caveats: Human pharmacology, dosing and safety are unknown. The compound is unapproved, sold as a research chemical or supplement of uncertain purity, and its long-term effects on methylation and NAD metabolism have not been evaluated.
deepLead:
5-Amino-1MQ (5-amino-1-methylquinolinium) is a small-molecule inhibitor of nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT), an enzyme involved in cellular NAD+ and methyl-group metabolism. It carries a permanent positive charge and is therefore handled as a salt, usually the chloride or iodide. Wikipedia notes that it has been sold as a gray-market weight-loss product, sometimes described as a peptide, although it is an experimental small molecule and not a peptide.
Research on it consists of cell and mouse experiments. In a 2018 mouse study, membrane-permeable NNMT inhibitors of this chemical family reversed diet-induced obesity. Wikipedia states that no formal toxicity studies or human clinical trial results exist. The compound is not an approved medicine.
In online communities it is discussed as an oral or injectable fat-loss and metabolism product, an extrapolation from the rodent findings rather than from human data.

name: Berberine

chain: Less fat gain, better nutrient partitioning
angle.text: Berberine is a plant alkaloid users call "nature's metformin", taking it to cut body fat, improve nutrient partitioning during bulks, and sometimes calm acne. Trials show modest effects on glucose, lipids and weight. Acne and partitioning claims are largely anecdotal.

summary: "Nature's metformin" — modest effects on glucose and lipid metabolism.
currentQuick:
Berberine is a yellow isoquinoline alkaloid found in plants such as goldenseal, barberry and Oregon grape, long used in traditional medicine. It is sold as a supplement and nicknamed nature's metformin because of its effects on blood glucose.
In fat-loss and looksmaxxing contexts it is used for appetite and metabolic support. Meta-analyses report modest improvements in glucose, lipids and sometimes body weight, though many trials are small and of uneven quality.
How it works: Berberine activates AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), the same cellular energy sensor engaged by metformin, and it inhibits mitochondrial complex I. It also influences hepatic glucose production, lipid metabolism, and gut microbiota. Its oral bioavailability is poor, so much of its action may depend on gut effects.
Risks and caveats: Gastrointestinal upset such as cramping, diarrhoea and constipation is the most common problem. It inhibits several CYP enzymes and transporters and may interact with drugs including ciclosporin and some diabetes medicines, and it is generally avoided in pregnancy and in newborns because of jaundice concerns. It is sold as a supplement in most countries, so product quality varies.
deepLead:
Berberine is a yellow quaternary ammonium alkaloid of the benzylisoquinoline class found in the roots, bark and stems of plants such as barberry (Berberis vulgaris), tree turmeric, Oregon grape, goldenseal and Chinese goldthread. Plants containing it have a long history in traditional medicine, and extracts are sold as dietary supplements. Wikipedia notes that, outside China where it is an over-the-counter drug for diarrhea, berberine is not approved as a prescription medicine in any country.
In appearance and body-composition communities it is used for appetite, blood sugar and nutrient-partitioning goals and is nicknamed "nature's metformin" because it activates the same energy-sensing enzyme, AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), that metformin engages. An umbrella review of 11 meta-analyses of randomized trials reported that berberine was associated with improvements in blood glucose, insulin resistance, lipids, body parameters and inflammatory markers compared with controls, while noting that the methodological quality of the meta-analyses needed improvement.
The most common adverse effects are gastrointestinal. Berberine inhibits the drug-metabolising enzyme CYP3A4 and has been reported to raise concentrations of ciclosporin and midazolam, and the US FDA issued warning letters to supplement makers about berberine marketing claims between 2020 and 2022.

name: L-Carnitine

angle.text: Users take L-carnitine as a fat burner and recovery aid, sometimes injected. It is promoted for shifting fat into energy use. Trials show small and inconsistent weight effects in most healthy people; injected versions and recovery claims rest mainly on anecdote.

summary: Shuttles fatty acids into mitochondria; modest and inconsistent weight effects.
currentQuick:
L-carnitine is a compound synthesised in the liver and kidneys from lysine and methionine and obtained from foods such as red meat. It is sold as a supplement, often in the forms L-carnitine tartrate or acetyl-L-carnitine, for fat loss, exercise recovery and energy.
Its physiological role is well established, but supplementation in people who are not deficient has produced modest and inconsistent effects on weight and body composition across meta-analyses.
How it works: Carnitine carries long-chain fatty acids across the inner mitochondrial membrane so they can be oxidised for energy, and it buffers excess acetyl groups. Oral supplementation raises plasma levels but does not reliably raise muscle carnitine in healthy people without additional measures, which may explain the weak results.
Risks and caveats: Intakes of about 2 to 3 g daily are generally tolerated, with nausea, diarrhoea and a fishy body odour at higher intakes. Gut bacteria convert carnitine to trimethylamine, which the liver turns into TMAO, a compound associated with cardiovascular risk in observational studies, though causality is unresolved. It is sold as a supplement and is unscheduled in most places.
deepLead:
L-Carnitine is the biologically active form of carnitine, a quaternary ammonium compound derived from amino acids that carries long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria so they can be oxidised for energy. It is concentrated in skeletal and cardiac muscle. Healthy people, including strict vegetarians, generally make enough of it in the body, and it was first extracted from meat in 1905, which gave it its name from the Latin for flesh.
It is sold as a supplement in oral, liquid and injectable forms and is used by athletes and dieters for fat loss, exercise performance and recovery. Wikipedia states that the quality of clinical research for these uses has been low, preventing firm conclusions. A 2020 meta-analysis of 37 randomized trials with 2,292 participants reported small average reductions in body weight, body mass index and fat mass.
Intake of carnitine has also been the subject of research on gut-bacteria-derived trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), a compound that has been linked in observational and animal work to cardiovascular risk.

name: EGCG

chain: Green tea catechin raises metabolism slightly
angle.text: EGCG is a green tea extract that users take as a fat burner, often before workouts, and some speculate about muscle effects via myostatin. Studies show small thermogenic effects with mixed results. The muscle-building claim is based on lab findings and anecdote.

summary: Small thermogenic and lipid-metabolism effects. Mixed data.
currentQuick:
Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) is the most abundant catechin in green tea and a polyphenol with antioxidant properties. It is sold as a concentrated extract in fat-burner and weight-management products, typically alongside caffeine.
Trials and meta-analyses of green tea catechins on weight and fat mass show small effects at best, with inconsistent results and strong dependence on caffeine intake and baseline habits.
How it works: EGCG may modestly raise energy expenditure and fat oxidation by inhibiting catechol-O-methyltransferase, which prolongs noradrenaline signalling, and may reduce fat absorption in the gut. Its effects in cells involve many pathways, but these have not translated to clear clinical results in people.
Risks and caveats: Concentrated green tea extracts, especially taken on an empty stomach, have been linked to liver injury in rare cases, and the European Food Safety Authority has set a caution level for catechin intake from supplements. EGCG can also reduce the absorption of iron and interact with some drugs. It is sold as a supplement; beverage tea is considered safe.
deepLead:
Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG, epigallocatechin-3-gallate) is the most abundant catechin in tea, an ester of epigallocatechin and gallic acid. It occurs at high levels in dried green tea leaves (about 7,380 mg per 100 g), white tea and, in smaller amounts, black tea, and is sold in concentrated form in many dietary supplements.
In physique and fat-loss circles it is taken as a fat-burner or pre-workout ingredient, often alongside caffeine-based thermogenics and L-carnitine, and some forum users have speculated about effects on myostatin. Wikipedia describes EGCG as heavily studied in basic research with various biological effects in the laboratory, while the human evidence for specific health claims is limited.
Safety is a documented concern at high doses: the European Food Safety Authority stated in 2018 that a daily intake of 800 mg or more of EGCG from supplements could raise the risk of liver damage, and the US FDA issued warning letters to EGCG supplement makers between 2008 and 2017 over disease claims and quality control.

name: Capsaicin

angle.text: Capsaicin from chili peppers appears in fat-loss diets and supplements, where users take it for a small metabolic and appetite boost. It is also tied to lip plumping and facial leanness discussions. Human studies show slight effects on energy use; the appearance claims are anecdotal.

summary: Chili compound; slight nudges to energy expenditure and appetite.
currentQuick:
Capsaicin is the pungent compound in chili peppers, best known as the agent that produces heat and as the active ingredient in topical pain creams and pepper sprays. It is also sold in capsule form as a thermogenic and appetite supplement.
In small human studies it modestly raises energy expenditure and fat oxidation and may lower appetite. Meta-analyses of its effect on body weight show small or inconsistent benefits that have not been shown to be noticeable in body appearance.
How it works: Capsaicin activates the TRPV1 ion channel on sensory neurons, triggering sympathetic nervous system activity and increased catecholamine release, which raises thermogenesis slightly. It may also affect satiety signalling and brown adipose tissue activity.
Risks and caveats: Oral use can cause stomach pain, burning, nausea and diarrhoea, and it may worsen reflux. Topical capsaicin causes burning and irritation, and contact with eyes or broken skin is painful. It is legal and unscheduled in food and supplement form.
deepLead:
Capsaicin (8-methyl-N-vanillyl-6-nonenamide) is the main pungent compound in chili peppers. It and related capsaicinoids are produced by plants of the genus Capsicum, likely as a deterrent to mammals and fungi, and it causes a burning sensation on contact with tissues in mammals.
It has two main relevant uses. As a prescription topical, a high-concentration (8%) patch (Qutenza) was approved by the US FDA and in the European Union in 2009 for pain from post-herpetic neuralgia and has since been studied in diabetic neuropathy. In the fat-loss and supplement market, capsaicin and chili extracts are included in thermogenic products on the premise that they raise energy expenditure and fat oxidation or reduce appetite; Wikipedia reports that as of 2007 there was no evidence weight loss was directly correlated with ingesting it, and that a 2014 meta-analysis found weak evidence that taking it before a meal might slightly reduce food intake.
Capsaicin acts by binding the TRPV1 receptor on pain-sensing neurons, work that contributed to the 2021 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

name: Creatine monohydrate

angle.text: Users take creatine to train harder and build muscle and strength, and it is a baseline supplement in physique-focused circles. Its muscle and strength effects are among the best studied of any supplement. Claims that it causes hair loss via DHT or kidney damage are debated and less well supported.

summary: The most proven supplement in existence: strength, size, high-intensity performance.
currentQuick:
Creatine monohydrate is the most widely studied sports supplement. Creatine itself is a nitrogen-containing compound made in the body from amino acids and also obtained from meat and fish; the monohydrate salt is the standard supplemental form. It is sold as a low-cost, flavourless powder.
In physique and performance circles it is used to support strength, lean mass gain during resistance training and repeated high-intensity effort. Many randomized trials and position stands report modest but consistent gains in these outcomes, and the wiki's evidence rating for it is strong.
How it works: Muscle stores creatine mostly as phosphocreatine, which rapidly regenerates ATP during short, intense efforts. Supplementation raises intramuscular creatine content, which researchers say can allow slightly more training work to be done and may encourage greater adaptation over time. Part of the early scale-weight increase is attributed to water drawn into muscle cells.
Risks and caveats: Creatine is legal and sold over the counter. Reviews of long-term use in healthy people have found it generally well tolerated, with water retention and occasional gastrointestinal upset the most commonly reported complaints. It can modestly raise serum creatinine without necessarily reflecting kidney damage, which can complicate lab interpretation, and people with kidney disease are advised to seek medical advice first. Responses vary and some people are reported as non-responders.
deepLead:
Creatine is an organic compound that helps regenerate adenosine triphosphate (ATP) in muscle and brain tissue. Its phosphorylated form, phosphocreatine, donates a phosphate group to ADP in a reaction catalysed by creatine kinase. The body makes it from glycine and arginine in the liver and kidneys, and about 95 percent of total body creatine sits in skeletal muscle. Creatine monohydrate is the most widely sold supplemental form.
It is among the most researched sports supplements. Wikipedia reports that supplementation raises muscle phosphocreatine stores, enhances short bursts of high-intensity exercise and supports strength adaptations, with a 2018 review in the Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition naming creatine monohydrate the most effective supplement for increasing high-intensity exercise capacity and muscle mass during training. A 2024 meta-analysis of resistance-training trials in adults under 50 found greater upper- and lower-body strength gains with creatine than placebo.
In looksmaxxing and physique communities it is used for muscle size and fullness, and it is also the subject of recurring questions about hair loss, kidney effects and whether it counts as a steroid. Researchers have examined each of these.

name: Whey protein

angle.text: Users take whey to hit protein targets, build muscle, and support leaner physiques while dieting. Muscle gain from adequate protein is well studied. Some forum posters link whey to acne, an association that has some observational support but limited controlled trials.

summary: Fast-digesting protein loaded with leucine for muscle protein synthesis.
currentQuick:
Whey protein is the liquid fraction of milk left over from cheese making, dried into concentrate, isolate or hydrolysate powders. It is a complete protein that digests quickly and is rich in leucine and other essential amino acids.
Lifters and dieters use it as a convenient way to reach daily protein targets, preserve lean mass while cutting and support muscle gain alongside resistance training. Meta-analyses report a small to moderate benefit for strength and lean mass, larger in older adults and in people who otherwise eat little protein.
How it works: Whey supplies a rapid rise in blood amino acids, particularly leucine, which stimulates muscle protein synthesis through mTORC1 signalling. Researchers attribute the benefit mainly to adding to total daily protein, so the advantage over other complete protein sources is reported as small when overall intake is already adequate.
Risks and caveats: Whey is a food product and legal everywhere. Lactose intolerance or milk allergy can cause digestive symptoms or reactions, and isolates contain less lactose. Quality control varies by brand, with occasional heavy-metal or labelling concerns reported. Studies have found no added benefit from very high intakes, and people with kidney disease are advised to follow medical guidance.
deepLead:
Whey protein is a mixture of proteins isolated from whey, the liquid by-product of cheese making. Its main components are beta-lactoglobulin, alpha-lactalbumin, serum albumin and immunoglobulins, and it is sold mainly as a powdered protein supplement in concentrate, isolate and hydrolysate forms.
It is used chiefly to support muscle growth and recovery after resistance training. A 2018 meta-analysis of 49 trials with 1,863 participants found that protein supplementation during prolonged resistance training modestly increased strength, fat-free mass and muscle size, with smaller effects on fat-free mass in older participants. A 2024 network meta-analysis of 116 trials examined how timing and protein type affect results. In 2010 a European Food Safety Authority panel concluded there was no evidence supporting weight-loss claims for whey and that it is roughly as effective as other protein sources for building strength and lean mass.
Reviews of adverse effects associate chronic, excessive use with possible kidney, liver, acne and microbiota concerns, while other researchers have argued that some of these claims are unsubstantiated.

name: Leucine

angle.text: Users add leucine to drinks or meals because it triggers muscle growth signaling, and compare protein sources by leucine content. Acute signaling is well studied; whether extra leucine beyond adequate protein adds measurable muscle is less clear.

summary: The amino acid that triggers muscle growth signaling (mTOR).
currentQuick:
Leucine is an essential branched-chain amino acid found in all dietary proteins, with especially high amounts in dairy, meat, eggs and soy. It is also sold as a standalone powder or as part of BCAA and essential amino acid products.
In the muscle-building context it is used to stimulate muscle protein synthesis, particularly in older adults or in people eating little protein. The wiki's strong rating reflects solid mechanistic and acute-response data; research indicates that extra isolated leucine adds little for people who already eat enough complete protein.
How it works: Leucine acts as a signal of amino acid availability. Sensors such as Sestrin2 respond to intracellular leucine and release inhibition of the mTORC1 complex, which promotes translation initiation and muscle protein synthesis. Insulin release triggered by leucine contributes to the same pathway.
Risks and caveats: Leucine is a normal dietary component and legal. High supplemental doses can cause digestive upset and may disturb the balance of other branched-chain amino acids, and leucine is hazardous for people with maple syrup urine disease. Long-term muscle-growth benefits from isolated leucine in healthy, well-fed trainees have not been well demonstrated.
deepLead:
Leucine is an essential branched-chain amino acid (BCAA): the human body cannot make it, so it must come from dietary protein such as meat, dairy, soy and legumes . Along with isoleucine and valine it is one of the three BCAAs, and it is sold both as a stand-alone powder and as an ingredient in BCAA, essential amino acid and pre- or intra-workout products.
In muscle-building communities leucine is discussed as the amino acid that most directly switches on muscle protein synthesis, through activation of the mTOR signalling pathway . Laboratory work has identified several intracellular leucine sensors, including Sestrin2 and SAR1B, that feed into mTORC1 .
Human trials show that protein supplementation in general modestly increases gains in lean mass and strength during resistance training . Evidence that adding isolated leucine to an already adequate protein intake produces further gains in healthy trainees is limited; most clinical work on leucine-enriched products has been done in older adults with sarcopenia, with mixed results .

name: Beta-alanine

angle.text: Beta-alanine is a pre-workout ingredient users take to get more work from high-rep sets, which they expect to translate to more muscle. It is studied for high-intensity performance gains. Direct effects on muscle size are less established; the tingling is a known harmless side effect.

summary: Buffers muscle acid for better high-rep performance. The tingles are normal.
currentQuick:
Beta-alanine is a non-proteinogenic amino acid and the rate-limiting building block of carnosine, a dipeptide stored in skeletal muscle. It is sold as a powder or capsule, often in pre-workout blends.
Athletes use it to improve performance in efforts lasting roughly one to four minutes and to get more work done in high-repetition sets. Studies report a modest effect that does not directly add muscle; the evidence base supports it as an ergogenic aid, and the wiki's rating is strong.
How it works: Taking beta-alanine for several weeks raises muscle carnosine content. Carnosine helps buffer hydrogen ions that accumulate during intense exercise, which is proposed to delay fatigue. The familiar tingling (paraesthesia) comes from activation of sensory nerve receptors and is not considered an indicator of effect.
Risks and caveats: Paraesthesia is the main reported side effect and is described as harmless, though uncomfortable to some; divided or slow-release forms reduce it. Beta-alanine is legal and not banned in sport. Long-term data in healthy adults show no clear toxicity at studied intakes. Studies have found little effect on single-effort maximal strength, with benefits reported mainly for high-rep and endurance-type work.
deepLead:
Beta-alanine is a naturally occurring non-proteinogenic amino acid in which the amino group sits on the beta carbon (IUPAC name 3-aminopropanoic acid) . It is the rate-limiting precursor of carnosine, a dipeptide stored at high concentration in skeletal muscle, where it acts as an intramuscular buffer . As a supplement it is sold as a powder or capsule and is a staple ingredient of pre-workout formulas.
It is used mainly in efforts lasting roughly 0.5 to 10 minutes and in high-repetition training, on the reasoning that more carnosine buffers hydrogen ions and delays neuromuscular fatigue . Its best-known acute effect is paraesthesia, a dose-dependent tingling sensation of the skin .
Meta-analyses of placebo-controlled trials report small average benefits for exercise capacity, concentrated in efforts of about one to four minutes, with less consistent results for maximal-intensity and very short efforts . It is not an agent that directly builds muscle tissue, and it is discussed in muscle-building communities chiefly as a performance and training-volume aid.

name: HMB

angle.text: HMB is used by lifters wanting to preserve muscle during cuts and recover faster, and is sometimes called a steroid alternative. Studies show benefits mainly in untrained or older people or during illness; effects in trained lifters are mixed and the steroid comparison is unsupported.

summary: Leucine metabolite studied for reducing muscle breakdown. Mixed results.
currentQuick:
HMB (beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate) is a metabolite of leucine, sold as a calcium salt or free acid. It originated in studies of reducing muscle breakdown and has been used by lifters during hard training or calorie restriction.
Results depend heavily on who is studied. Meta-analyses suggest it helps preserve muscle in older adults and in clinical settings, while trials in trained young athletes mostly show little effect; the wiki's rating is moderate.
How it works: HMB is thought to reduce protein breakdown through effects on the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway and to modestly support protein synthesis signalling and muscle cell repair. Human data for these mechanisms are less consistent than animal and cell work.
Risks and caveats: HMB is legal and has a good short-term safety record in trials. Reported side effects are minor, mostly gastrointestinal. Trials in experienced trainees eating enough protein and training progressively have generally not found clear benefits, and product quality is reported to vary.
deepLead:
HMB (beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate) is a metabolite of the essential amino acid leucine that the body produces naturally; roughly 5 percent of dietary leucine is converted to it. Two supplement forms have been studied, a calcium salt (HMB-Ca) and a free acid (HMB-FA) .
It is marketed to lifters and athletes for reducing muscle damage and muscle protein breakdown and for supporting recovery, and it is also used in clinical oral nutritional supplements for older and ill patients .
The research picture differs by population. The International Society of Sports Nutrition (ISSN) position stand states that HMB's proposed mode of action is a dual effect, enhancing muscle protein synthesis and suppressing breakdown, and that chronic intake appears safe for up to at least a year . Meta-analyses in trained athletes report small effects, while results in older adults and in clinical conditions are more often positive but vary by study .

name: Citrulline malate

chain: Boosts nitric oxide and blood flow
angle.text: Users take citrulline malate in pre-workouts for a muscle pump and more reps, and some pair it with tadalafil for blood flow. Studies on reps and endurance are mixed, and the pump's effect on long-term muscle growth is untested.

summary: Nitric-oxide precursor for pump and blood flow; performance data mixed.
currentQuick:
Citrulline malate combines the amino acid L-citrulline with malic acid. Citrulline is an intermediate of the urea cycle and a precursor of arginine, and is a common ingredient in pre-workout powders.
It is used for muscle pump, endurance in resistance sets and reduced soreness. Meta-analyses report a small improvement in repetitions to failure with low certainty, and single trials often show no effect.
How it works: Citrulline is converted to arginine in the kidney, which raises nitric oxide production and blood vessel dilation. It may also help clear ammonia and lactate-related fatigue, and malate may feed energy metabolism, though these steps have not been firmly established for performance.
Risks and caveats: Citrulline malate is legal and generally well tolerated; the main reported complaint is stomach upset at larger amounts. It can lower blood pressure slightly, which is relevant for people taking antihypertensive or erectile dysfunction drugs. Benefits for muscle size have not been established.
deepLead:
Citrulline malate (CM) is a supplement that combines the amino acid L-citrulline with malic acid. Citrulline is a non-essential alpha-amino acid and a key intermediate in the urea cycle, the pathway mammals use to convert ammonia to urea; it is also a byproduct of nitric oxide production from arginine . Its name comes from citrullus, the Latin word for watermelon, from which it was first isolated in 1914 .
CM is a common ingredient in pre-workout powders, where it is promoted for muscle 'pump', blood flow, endurance in resistance sets and recovery . The proposed mechanism is increased nitric oxide and blood flow to active muscle, with possible effects on ammonia handling and on ATP production through malate .
Published evidence on exercise performance is described by reviewers as equivocal . Wikipedia states that there is no good evidence that taking citrulline is effective or safe for athletic performance and that it has no confirmed clinical uses . No study in the sources reviewed here has shown that CM increases muscle size.
